purpose: Definitive, MEASURED set of twoway options that Stata accepts and dash rejects. Counter-example set for the dash.sthlp:668-673 claim that "No error is produced for unknown options, so existing Stata graph commands copy-pasted into dash will still run".

method.per_probe: 1) run `twoway <spec>, <opts> nodraw` under -capture- and record rc; a non-zero rc means the probe is not legal Stata and was fixed, not recorded. 2) `dash clear`. 3) run `dash <spec>, <opts> name(g1)` under -capture noisily- and record rc plus the exact error line. 4) on success, record ${dash_json_g1}, the spec JSON handed to dash_render.py.
method.attribution: Where Stata requires a companion option (droplines needs range(); clegend needs colorvar(); mlabangle needs mlabel(); colorlist needs colordiscrete), the companion is passed to twoway ONLY, so the dash side sees the option under test alone and the dash rc is attributable to exactly one option key.
method.controls: 41 zero-option plottype controls establish the per-plottype baseline, so a non-zero dash rc below is attributable to the option and not to the plottype.

environment.data: sysuse auto (cross-sectional probes); synthetic 60-month tsset panel (t* probes)

root_cause: dash.ado:230 (_dash_parse_graph_opts) and dash.ado:293 (_dash_parse_plot_opts) are closed `syntax [, ...]` allow-lists. Neither call site wraps them in -capture-, and neither declares a catch-all, so any option key outside the list makes -syntax- exit r(198) "option X() not allowed" and abort the calling do-file. The help text is false by construction, not by accident.

blocking_defects.summary: Any do-file whose effective `version` is 17.0 or lower cannot register ANY dash graph. _dash_register_graph (dash.ado:857) validates the graph name with regexm("`name'", "^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,31}$"). The {0,31} interval quantifier is only understood by the regex engine Stata selects under version >= 18, so under version <= 17 regexm() returns 0 for a legal name such as g1 and dash exits r(198) "dash: invalid graph name". dash.ado itself declares `version 16.0`, i.e. the package's own declared minimum version is one under which it cannot function at all. The same regex appears twice (dash.ado:857 for `dash <spec>, name()` and dash.ado:1088 for `dash kpi ..., name()`), so KPI tiles are blocked too.
blocking_defects.note: This must be measured with STRAIGHT-LINE `version` statements. Inside a -foreach- loop the body is compiled under the ambient version, so c(version) reads 16 while regexm() still uses the new engine and the bug hides. Section 26 of the corpus does it straight-line.

dash_only_note: Section 27 of the corpus. Keys dash accepts that real twoway does not have (twoway_rc==198): mlabwidth, malpha, lalpha, falpha, jseed, colpalette, colornlevels, colormissing, marker, plotbgcolor, link, filter, and the secondary-axis *2 family. Three of the suspects turned out to BE real twoway options (blcolor, bfcolor, bgcolor), so they are not dash-only. Where dash invented a spelling for something Stata already names -- jseed vs Stata jitterseed, colornlevels vs colorlevels, colormissing vs colorformissing -- the Stata spelling appears in rejected_options above, so a user gets neither the feature nor a working copy-paste.

rejected_syntax_constructs.reason: dash's own help documents the y= form and dash.ado:630 strips a leading 'y=' -- but the strip runs AFTER _dash_parse_varpart_any, whose `syntax anything(name=vals)` rejects the '=' first. `dash function y=x` dies with r(101) '=exp not allowed'; only the bare `dash function x` form works.
Weighted twoway plots abort with r(101) "weights not allowed". Weights are extremely common in copy-pasted twoway code.

rejected_syntax_constructs.dash_message: dash: invalid graph name 'g1, replace'. Names must start with a letter or under score and contain only letters, digits, and underscores (max 32 chars).
rejected_syntax_constructs.reason: dash.sthlp documents name(name, replace) and _dash_register_graph (dash.ado:867) explicitly greps the raw spec for it -- but the name-format check at dash.ado:857 runs first on the whole string 'g1, replace' and rejects it with r(198). The documented replace sub-option is unreachable.

accepted_but_discarded.effect: CORRUPTED, not merely dropped. title() is declared `string` (not `asis`), so -syntax- strips the quotes and dash re-joins the remainder: the spec carries title="T , size(large)" and the rendered Bokeh figure title literally reads `T , size(large)`.
accepted_but_discarded.verified_by: Rendered abd.html and found the exact text node "T , size(large)" as the figure title.

accepted_but_discarded.effect: DROPPED. The string survives into the spec as legend="order(1 2)", but dash_render.py:6283 only understands off/on/ring/top/bottom/left/right, label(N "txt"), cols(#) and rows(#). order() is never parsed; the substring "order(1 2)" does not appear anywhere in the rendered HTML, and legend item order is whatever the plot layers happen to be in.

DROPPED. Spec carries ylabel=", format(%9.0fc)". DashRenderer._parse_axis_label_opt() returns ([], {}) for it, so no FixedTicker and no formatter is attached and the axis keeps Bokeh default numbering. Only xlabel()/ylabel() angle() is honoured from the sub-option block.
DROPPED. Spec carries xlabel="#10"; the parser accepts only bare numbers and quoted labels, so #10 yields ([], {}) and the "about 10 ticks" request is lost.
DROPPED. Spec carries xlabel="minmax"; parser yields ([], {}).

DROPPED. Spec carries xlabel="1990(5)2020"; the parser has no numlist expander, so a Stata range-with-step -- the single most common xlabel() form -- yields ([], {}). Note xlabel(10 20 30) (explicit list) DOES work, which makes the failure silent and inconsistent.
DROPPED. Spec carries yscale="range(0 50)". dash_render.py:_parse_scale_opt() extracts only the words "log" and "reverse"; range() is never read, no Range1d is created, and the axis autoscales.
accepted_but_discarded.verified_by: Executed _parse_scale_opt("range(0 50)") -> (False, False); rendered abd.html contains no Range1d model instance and no end:50.
